author: worker_1
belief: As of 2014, the electric chair was an optional form of execution in Alabama. Inmates could choose electrocution as an alternative to the default lethal injection method.

author: worker_2
object: Florida electric chair status as of 2014
belief: As of 2014, Florida allowed the electric chair as an optional form of execution. Florida Statute 922.105 provided that death sentences would be carried out by lethal injection unless the inmate affirmatively elected to be executed by electrocution.

author: worker_3
object: South Carolina execution method law in 2014
belief: In 2014, South Carolina allowed inmates to choose between lethal injection and electrocution (electric chair). Lethal injection became the primary method in 1995, but inmates retained the option to elect electrocution instead. This was confirmed by multiple sources stating that "inmates had the option of lethal injection or electrocution" prior to the 2021 law change.

author: worker_4
belief: As of 2014, Idaho's only execution method was lethal injection. The electric chair was not an authorized or optional method of execution in Idaho in 2014. Idaho switched from hanging to lethal injection in 1978, and never adopted the electric chair as a method.
